title: Soft-commit protocol for interrupted streaming generations and client backpressure arbitration
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Problem: client disconnects and timing-related aborts currently cause either full garbage collection of partial generations (losing useful prefixes) or indefinite retention of large KV caches (memory/cost pressure). We need a middle-ground policy that preserves resumeability for likely-to-reconnect clients while bounding resource usage and respecting backpressure signals from the serving runtime.

Goal: define and implement a ‘soft-commit’ lifecycle for interrupted streaming generations: persist minimal resume metadata + compacted prefix, integrate this with adaptive backpressure arbitration (server-initiated eviction vs client grace window), and add KV-cache trimming heuristics that prioritize useful prefixes for resumption. This should improve user-facing resume success rate and reduce memory churn under transient disconnects without increasing tail latency under load.
acceptance_criteria: Define protocol messages for soft-commit and resume handshake (spec doc linked)
Server can persist compacted resume metadata and a prefix snapshot (<= configurable bytes) for interrupted generations
KV cache trimming reduces memory footprint by >= 35% on synthetic reconnect workload without decreasing resume success rate below 90%
Soft-commit lifecycle has configurable grace window and observed P95 latency delta < 5% in our canary cluster
End-to-end tests for resume handshake, double-reconnects, and race with model-eviction pass in CI
technical_notes: Soft-commit stores: (a) compacted prefix tokens (configurable max_bytes), (b) small resume fingerprint + generation cursor, (c) light tombstone with lease expiration and reconnection hint
Lease model: generation owner has active lease; on disconnect we drop to soft-commit (short lease) then hard GC after grace_window if no reconnect
Backpressure arbitration: when memory pressure high, server may reduce grace_window for low-utility prefixes (heuristic below)
KV trimming heuristic: LRU by (last-accessed, prefix-length, model-size) with bias to keep prefixes that enabled >=1 successful resume in last 24h
Compatibility: protocol must be compatible with existing SDK streaming resume handshake; fallback to current behavior if client SDK doesn’t implement resume
decisions: Persist compacted prefix (tokenized + gzip) instead of full token stream — reduces storage/memory overhead and privacy surface
Grace window default: 45s for general tier, 180s for enterprise/dedicated tenants (configurable per-tenant)
Make soft-commit state eviction policy server-configurable and visible in Console under stream lifecycle dashboards
Do not change default client SDK behavior — introduce opt-in resume flag in SDK v2.4 to enable soft-commit-enabled resumable streams
next_steps: Finalize protocol spec and add message samples: done (spec PR open)
Implement server-side soft-commit state machine and KV-trim hook (work in branch: feature/soft-commit)
Add metrics + dashboard: resume_attempts, resume_success_rate, soft_commit_retained_bytes, soft_commit_evictions
Canary rollout plan: 1) internal canary in us-west-2 with 10% traffic, 2) opt-in beta customers, 3) global rollout after 3 weeks of stable metrics
Add end-to-end tests and chaos test: random disconnects, reconnect jitter, and memory pressure injection

2026-02-25 — Security review (Sandra Liu): No sensitive artifacts persisted in compacted prefix (we gzip token IDs only). Recommend a KMS rotation checklist for any future persisted state — tracked separately.
